Cloud discovery finds Shadow IT, the apps people use without IT approval, by analyzing firewall and proxy traffic logs, or Defender for Endpoint signals, against a catalog of more than 31,000 cloud apps that are each scored on many risk factors. Apps can then be marked sanctioned or unsanctioned. For connected apps it can scan files, apply sensitivity labels and remove risky external sharing, and SSPM reports app misconfigurations into Microsoft Secure Score.

concepts.heading: Session Control and App Governance
concepts.body: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access decides whether a user may sign in. Conditional Access app control in Defender for Cloud Apps controls what happens after sign-in. Access policies decide who may open an app, for example blocking access from unmanaged devices. Session policies monitor and control the session in real time, for example blocking downloads of sensitive files to unmanaged devices or blocking uploads of malware. Edge users get in-browser protection and other browsers are routed through a reverse proxy, so nothing needs to be installed on the device, which suits contractors and personal laptops. App governance covers a different risk: OAuth apps that users have allowed to read their mail or files. It shows these apps, their permissions and data access, flags unused or overprivileged apps and expiring credentials, and detects and responds to suspicious app behavior.

concepts.heading: Microsoft Defender for Identity
concepts.body: Microsoft Defender for Identity detects, investigates and responds to identity-based attacks across on-premises, cloud and hybrid environments, using signals from on-premises Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID and other identity providers. Its sensors run on identity infrastructure: domain controllers, AD FS, AD CS and Microsoft Entra Connect servers. They parse network traffic and Windows events locally and send only the needed signals to the cloud. Detections follow the stages of an identity attack: reconnaissance such as enumerating users and groups, compromised credentials such as brute force, lateral movement toward sensitive accounts, and domain dominance such as DCShadow or Golden Ticket activity. Do not confuse it with Microsoft Entra ID Protection, which calculates user risk and sign-in risk for cloud sign-ins that Conditional Access can act on. A hybrid company uses both, and both feed Defender XDR incidents.

concepts.heading: Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management
concepts.body: Every large estate has more vulnerabilities than a team can patch at once. Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management provides continuous asset discovery and inventories of software, certificates, hardware, firmware and browser extensions, then ranks weaknesses by real risk using Microsoft threat intelligence, breach likelihood, business context and device assessments. From a security recommendation, IT can create a remediation task in Microsoft Intune, block a vulnerable application or apply an alternate mitigation, and progress is tracked in real time. It covers Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS and network devices. Core capabilities, such as vulnerability and configuration assessment, risk-based prioritization and remediation tracking, are included in Defender for Endpoint Plan 2. Premium capabilities, such as security baselines assessment, browser extension and certificate assessment and blocking vulnerable apps, come with the add-on or the standalone offering.

concepts.heading: Microsoft Threat Intelligence
concepts.body: Microsoft Threat Intelligence is Microsoft's research on threat actors, campaigns, tools and vulnerabilities, drawn from the very large volume of signals Microsoft sees, and it is built into the Defender products. Threat analytics in the Defender portal is the most visible part: each report analyzes a tracked threat, such as a ransomware campaign or a critical vulnerability, gives guidance on how to defend against it, and adds data from your own environment, showing whether the threat is active there and whether the matching protections are in place. Intelligence also enriches entity pages for IP addresses, domains, URLs and files with reputation and related threat reports, helps Defender Vulnerability Management prioritize, and feeds automatic attack disruption. For example, after a news report on a new campaign, a security lead opens its threat analytics report to check exposure.

examPoints: A question that describes unapproved cloud apps found from firewall or proxy logs is testing cloud discovery, while blocking downloads on unmanaged devices during a session is testing Conditional Access app control.

A question that mentions domain controllers, lateral movement or Golden Ticket attacks is testing Defender for Identity, while risky cloud sign-ins that feed Conditional Access are testing Microsoft Entra ID Protection.

A question that asks which vulnerabilities to fix first with remediation through Intune is testing Defender Vulnerability Management, while Microsoft's analysis of a campaign and your exposure is testing threat analytics.

quiz.q: Microsoft Defender for Identity must be deployed before it can detect attacks on Active Directory. Where does it run its sensors?
choices: On every user's laptop, as part of the Microsoft Defender Antivirus client
On identity servers such as domain controllers, AD FS and Entra Connect
Inside each Microsoft 365 mailbox, alongside the anti-phishing policies
In the browser session, through a reverse proxy for unmanaged devices
quiz.explain: Defender for Identity sensors run on identity infrastructure such as domain controllers, AD FS, AD CS and Microsoft Entra Connect servers, where they read traffic and events. Choice A is tempting because many attacks start on laptops, but device telemetry is collected by Defender for Endpoint, not by Defender for Identity.

quiz.q: A company connects Salesforce and other SaaS apps to Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps. It wants to find risky settings inside those apps and see them in Microsoft Secure Score. Which capability is this?
choices: Cloud discovery, which scores apps from firewall and proxy traffic logs
App governance, which watches OAuth app permissions and credential use
Conditional Access app control, which limits downloads during a session
SaaS Security Posture Management, which reports app misconfigurations
quiz.explain: SSPM checks the configuration of connected SaaS apps and feeds its findings into Microsoft Secure Score. Choice A is tempting because cloud discovery also produces risk scores, but it rates which apps people use from traffic logs, not how your connected apps are configured.

days.recap: Defender for Cloud Apps is a CASB (discovery, session control, SSPM, app governance), Defender for Identity guards Active Directory from sensors on identity servers, Vulnerability Management ranks and remediates weaknesses, and Microsoft Threat Intelligence powers threat analytics.

days.title: Service Trust Portal, Privacy Principles, and Compliance Manager

concepts.heading: The Service Trust Portal
concepts.body: The Microsoft Service Trust Portal (STP) is where Microsoft publishes audit reports and other compliance information about its cloud services. Under the shared responsibility model a customer cannot audit Microsoft's datacenters itself, so it relies on reports from external auditors, such as ISO/IEC certificates and SOC 1, 2 and 3 reports. Some content is public, but many reports require signing in with a Microsoft Entra organization account and accepting the Non-Disclosure Agreement for Compliance Materials. Restricted documents also need a role such as Tenant Admin, Compliance Administrator, Security Administrator or Security Reader. Content is grouped into Certifications, Regulations, and Standards; Reports, Whitepapers, and Artifacts (for example BCP and DR, and pen test results); Industry and Regional Resources; and Resources for your Organization. My Library saves documents and can email you when they are updated.

concepts.heading: Microsoft's Privacy Principles
concepts.body: Learn says Microsoft's approach to privacy gives customers control over the data they put in the cloud, guaranteed through contractual commitments, and the Microsoft Trust Center outlines it across four areas. Data control: your data belongs to you, you can access, modify or delete it, Microsoft uses it only to provide the services you chose, and it is never mined for advertising or marketing research. Data location: in Azure, Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365 you can determine where data is stored, with data residency options around the world. Data security: data is encrypted at rest, with options up to AES-256, and in transit with TLS and IPsec, using two or more independent layers, and Azure Key Vault lets you control keys and secrets. Data defense: government requests should go to the customer, Microsoft gives no government direct access, notifies you where legally permitted and challenges unlawful demands.

concepts.heading: The Microsoft Purview Portal
concepts.body: Microsoft Purview is a family of solutions that help organizations govern, protect and manage data. The Microsoft Purview portal is the unified place to find and use its data security, data governance, and risk and compliance solutions, and a single entry point for settings, search, and roles and permissions. It replaced the retired Microsoft Purview compliance portal. The home page shows solution cards and a Compliance posture status section with summary information from Compliance Manager, such as completion rates for the top assessments. What each person sees depends on their permissions, granted through Purview role groups, and on the organization's subscription: an administrator without access to insider risk management simply does not see that card, and the card layout cannot be customized. From the portal you can also open related portals such as Microsoft Defender, Microsoft Entra and the Service Trust Portal.

concepts.heading: Compliance Manager
concepts.body: Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager helps an organization assess and manage compliance across a multicloud environment, from finding data protection risks to implementing controls and reporting to auditors. An assessment groups the controls of one regulation, standard or policy, and one assessment can cover several services, such as Microsoft 365, Azure, AWS and Google Cloud, with progress shown per service. Assessments are built from templates: the Data Protection Baseline is included at all subscription levels and sets the initial score, other regulations are premium templates, and custom templates are possible. Controls are Microsoft managed, your controls, or shared, depending on who implements them. Improvement actions give step-by-step guidance; you can assign an owner, upload evidence and have an assessor set the test status. Many actions are tested automatically with signals from Purview solutions, Microsoft Secure Score and Defender for Cloud.

concepts.heading: Compliance Score
concepts.body: The compliance score shown in Compliance Manager measures progress in completing improvement actions. It is risk-based: each action has a point value that reflects the risk it reduces. Mandatory actions cannot be bypassed by users, while discretionary actions rely on users following a policy; preventative actions stop risks, detective actions find them and corrective actions limit the damage. Learn's values make preventative mandatory actions worth 27 points, preventative discretionary 9, detective or corrective mandatory 3 and detective or corrective discretionary 1. The score helps you understand your current posture and prioritize the actions that reduce the most risk, and it is a good number to report to leadership. It is not a guarantee of compliance or a certificate: you must still validate your controls for your regulatory environment. Do not confuse it with Microsoft Secure Score, which measures security posture in the Defender portal.

examPoints: A question that asks where to download Microsoft's own SOC or ISO/IEC audit reports is testing the Service Trust Portal, while tracking the controls your organization must implement is testing Compliance Manager.

A question that describes in-country storage, government data requests, encryption or no advertising use is testing one of the four privacy areas: data location, data defense, data security or data control.

A question about which improvement action raises the compliance score most, or whether the score proves compliance, is testing risk-based points (preventative mandatory highest) and the rule that the score is not a guarantee.

quiz.q: Leaders ask whether a high compliance score in Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager means the company is certified under a regulation. What is the accurate answer?
choices: Yes, a high score is accepted by auditors as proof of certification on its own
Yes, because Microsoft managed controls cover every requirement automatically
No, it measures risk-weighted progress on improvement actions, not certification
No, because the score counts only the actions that Microsoft implements for you
quiz.explain: The compliance score tracks risk-weighted progress on improvement actions, and Learn states that Compliance Manager recommendations are not a guarantee of compliance. Choice B is tempting because Microsoft managed controls do add points, but the customer still owns its own controls and shares others, and auditors still assess them.

quiz.q: An auditor needs Microsoft's own ISO/IEC 27001 certificate for Microsoft 365, while the compliance team must track the controls the company itself implements for the same standard. Which pairing is correct?
choices: Certificate from the Service Trust Portal; own controls tracked in Compliance Manager
Certificate from Compliance Manager; own controls tracked in the Service Trust Portal
Both come from the Data Protection Baseline assessment on the Purview portal home page
Both come from the four privacy commitment areas published in the Microsoft Trust Center
quiz.explain: The Service Trust Portal publishes third-party audit reports about Microsoft's services, while Compliance Manager assessments track the customer's own and shared controls. Choice B is tempting because it names the right two tools, but it swaps their jobs.

days.recap: The Service Trust Portal holds Microsoft's audit reports, the privacy principles cover data control, location, security and defense, the Purview portal is the entry point, and Compliance Manager tracks assessments with a risk-based compliance score that is not a guarantee.

days.title: Information Protection, Data Lifecycle, Insider Risk, eDiscovery, and Audit

concepts.heading: Classifying Data and the Two Explorers
concepts.body: Purview identifies sensitive items in three ways: users label content manually, sensitive information types (SITs) recognize patterns such as credit card numbers with supporting evidence like keywords or a checksum, and trainable classifiers use machine learning to recognize document categories without a fixed pattern, such as contracts or résumés. Exact data match SITs match only values that really exist in your own table, such as your patients' record numbers. Two tools show the results. Content explorer answers what sensitive data you have and where: a current snapshot of items with sensitivity or retention labels or matching SITs and classifiers, grouped by location, with extra restricted roles to view the items themselves. Activity explorer answers what is being done with it: a history from the audit log, up to 30 days, of labels applied, changed or removed and DLP matches, including users' justifications for removing a label.

concepts.heading: Sensitivity Labels and Label Policies
concepts.body: A sensitivity label, such as Public, General, Confidential or Highly Confidential, classifies content and can protect it. It is stored in clear text in the file or email metadata, so it stays with the content wherever it goes, and if the label encrypts, only the people you chose can open the copy, even outside the organization. Labels can also add markings such as watermarks, headers and footers, be applied automatically when sensitive information is found, or, when scoped to groups and sites, control privacy and external access for Teams, Microsoft 365 Groups and SharePoint sites. Creating a label does not show it to anyone: a sensitivity label policy publishes labels to users and groups, and several policies let only the legal team see Highly Confidential. Policies also set a default label, mandatory labeling and justification for removing or downgrading a label.

concepts.heading: Data Loss Prevention
concepts.body: Data loss prevention (DLP) stops people from sharing sensitive data with those who should not have it. A DLP policy names what to look for, often a sensitive information type, the locations to watch, and the action to take. Locations include Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams chats and channels, Office apps, Windows and macOS endpoints and on-premises file shares. Actions range from a policy tip that warns the user, to blocking with an override that captures a business justification, to blocking with no override. Microsoft recommends deploying new policies in simulation mode first, checking their impact and then moving to more restrictive modes. DLP activity is recorded in the audit log and appears in Activity explorer. For example, a bank warns users who email credit card numbers to outside recipients and records the justification of anyone who overrides.

concepts.heading: Retention and Records Management
concepts.body: Data Lifecycle Management keeps what you must keep and deletes what you no longer need. A retention policy applies one setting to whole locations, such as every mailbox or a SharePoint site. A retention label applies at item level, travels with the item within Microsoft 365, and alone supports starting the period at an event such as an employee leaving, a disposition review before deletion, and marking an item as a record. Retention label policies publish labels to locations or apply them automatically. When settings conflict, retention wins over deletion and the longest retention period wins. Records management uses labels that declare a record, which blocks deletion (and editing while the record is locked) and keeps proof of disposition; a regulatory record cannot be removed even by an administrator. Preservation Lock makes a policy impossible to turn off or weaken, for rules that demand it.

concepts.heading: Insider Risk, eDiscovery, and Audit
concepts.body: Insider risk management detects risky patterns by an organization's own users, such as departing employees copying files to USB, from templates like Data theft by departing users, which is triggered by an HR connector or by deletion of the user's Microsoft Entra account. Users are pseudonymized by default, and cases can be escalated to eDiscovery. eDiscovery finds and delivers electronically stored information for legal cases: a case holds searches, holds that preserve content for that matter, and exports, and E5 premium features add review sets with analytics such as conversation threading and optical character recognition. The classic eDiscovery (Standard) and (Premium) experiences retired on August 31, 2025; the Purview portal now has one eDiscovery solution. Audit records user and admin activity in the unified audit log. Audit (Standard) is on by default with 180-day retention; Audit (Premium) adds one-year default retention for key services, custom retention policies and intelligent insights such as which mail items were accessed.

examPoints: A question that contrasts protecting content wherever it travels with keeping or deleting it for a period is testing sensitivity labels versus retention policies and labels.
A question that asks what sensitive data exists and where is testing Content explorer, while who changed or removed labels is testing Activity explorer.
A question about risky behavior by departing employees is testing insider risk management, preserving content for a lawsuit is testing eDiscovery holds, and finding who did what is testing Audit.

quiz.q: A company wants documents labeled Highly Confidential to stay encrypted even after they are emailed outside the organization, and separately wants all mailbox content kept for seven years. Which pairing is correct?
choices: A retention label for the encryption, and a sensitivity label for the seven years
A DLP policy for the encryption, and an eDiscovery case hold for all seven years
An insider risk policy for the encryption, and Audit (Premium) for the seven years
A sensitivity label for the encryption, and a retention policy for the seven years
quiz.explain: Sensitivity labels are stored in the file metadata and their encryption travels with the content, while a retention policy keeps everything in chosen locations such as all mailboxes. Choice A is tempting because it names two real label types, but it swaps their jobs: retention labels do not encrypt, and sensitivity labels do not set retention periods.

quiz.q: Microsoft Purview must find credit card numbers in documents. The numbers follow a fixed format and pass a checksum. Which classification method is designed for this?
choices: A trainable classifier built from hundreds of sample documents
A sensitive information type that matches a pattern and validates it
Content explorer, which lists every single file that a user has opened
A retention label that is applied automatically to every new file
quiz.explain: Sensitive information types look for a pattern, such as a card number format, and confirm it with supporting evidence like a checksum or nearby keywords. Choice A is tempting because trainable classifiers also classify content automatically, but they are meant for document categories that have no fixed pattern, such as contracts.

days.recap: Classify with SITs and trainable classifiers, see results in Content and Activity explorer, protect with sensitivity labels and DLP, keep or delete with retention policies and labels (records for locked items), and use insider risk, eDiscovery and Audit for people and investigations.

days.title: Final Review: Exam Format, Commonly Confused Pairs, and Test-Day Plan

concepts.heading: Know the Exam Format
concepts.body: SC-900 gives you 45 minutes for the assessment, and you pass with a scaled score of 700 or greater. Microsoft does not publish the number of questions, so pace yourself by time rather than by a fixed count. The domains are Describe the concepts of security, compliance, and identity at 10 to 15 percent, Describe the capabilities of Microsoft Entra at 25 to 30 percent, Describe the capabilities of Microsoft security solutions at 35 to 40 percent, and Describe the capabilities of Microsoft compliance solutions at 20 to 25 percent. The exam is proctored and may have interactive components; Microsoft does not list the question types in advance, but the Exam Sandbox on Learn lets you try them in the same interface. Most questions cover generally available features, so study current names such as Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft Defender XDR and Microsoft Purview. If the exam is not offered in your preferred language, you can request an extra 30 minutes.

concepts.heading: Confused Pairs: Concepts and Microsoft Entra
concepts.body: Authentication proves who you are; authorization decides what you may do. Encryption can be reversed with the right key, while hashing is one-way and is used to check that data has not changed or to store passwords. Defense in depth layers many controls, while Zero Trust says verify explicitly, use least privilege and assume breach. Microsoft Entra ID Protection calculates user and sign-in risk, while Conditional Access is the policy engine that acts on signals such as that risk to allow, block or require MFA. Microsoft Entra roles manage the directory and Microsoft 365 settings, while Azure RBAC manages Azure resources. Privileged Identity Management gives just-in-time, time-bound admin access, while access reviews periodically check who still needs access. Defender for Identity watches on-premises Active Directory, while ID Protection scores cloud sign-ins.

concepts.heading: Confused Pairs: Security Solutions
concepts.body: NSGs filter traffic to subnets and network interfaces by rules, Azure Firewall is a managed, stateful firewall for whole virtual networks, and Web Application Firewall protects web apps from attacks such as SQL injection; DDoS Protection absorbs flood attacks. Azure Bastion gives RDP and SSH through the browser without public IPs on VMs. In Defender for Cloud, CSPM recommends configuration fixes and builds the secure score, while workload protection plans raise alerts on attacks. Microsoft Sentinel is the SIEM and SOAR for the whole estate, while Defender XDR correlates Microsoft's own endpoint, identity, email and app products; both meet in the Defender portal. In Sentinel, automation rules handle incidents and playbooks act in other systems. Safe Attachments acts before delivery, Safe Links at the time of click and ZAP after delivery. Secure score in Defender for Cloud is not the same as Microsoft Secure Score in the Defender portal.

concepts.heading: Confused Pairs: Compliance Solutions
concepts.body: The Service Trust Portal holds Microsoft's own audit reports, while Compliance Manager tracks the controls you implement; compliance score measures progress on improvement actions and is not a guarantee. Sensitivity labels classify and protect content wherever it travels, while retention labels and policies decide how long content is kept; a retention policy covers whole locations and a retention label covers items and travels with them. DLP checks individual actions on sensitive data as they happen, while insider risk management looks for risky patterns in a person's behavior over time. Content explorer shows what sensitive data exists and where, while Activity explorer shows what people did with labeled content. An eDiscovery hold preserves content for one legal matter, while retention is a standing lifecycle rule. Audit records who did what; it does not block, encrypt or hold anything.

concepts.heading: Error Log, Test-Day Plan, and Retakes
concepts.body: For every practice question you miss or guess, write down the pair you confused, such as DLP versus insider risk, and the clue in the stem that should have decided it; the same confusions repeat, so reviewing them is faster than rereading every day. Spend the most time on the security solutions domain, the largest, unless your log shows another weak spot. On test day, check your room, webcam and system early for an online exam, read the instructions on each question, answer what you know first and mark uncertain items for review (after a break you cannot return to earlier questions). Choose exactly the number of answers requested, and answer every question, since there is no penalty for guessing. If you do not pass, you can retake after 24 hours; later attempts need 14 days between them, with at most five attempts in 12 months, and an exam you passed cannot be retaken unless the certification has expired.

examPoints: A question that lists Conditional Access, Entra ID Protection and Privileged Identity Management as choices is testing whether you can tell the policy engine, the risk calculator and just-in-time admin access apart.

A question that offers sensitivity labels, retention labels, DLP and insider risk management as choices is testing whether the need is protection, lifecycle, a single risky action, or a risky pattern of behavior.

quiz.q: A learner keeps mixing up Microsoft Entra Conditional Access and Microsoft Entra ID Protection. Which statement separates them correctly?
choices: Conditional Access calculates user risk, while ID Protection enforces the sign-in rules
ID Protection calculates user and sign-in risk, which Conditional Access policies can act on
Both are Microsoft Purview features that label each sign-in by its sensitivity level
Conditional Access protects only on-premises AD, while ID Protection protects only the mailboxes
quiz.explain: Entra ID Protection detects risks and calculates user and sign-in risk levels, and Conditional Access policies use those levels as signals to block access or require MFA or a password change. Choice A is tempting because it names both real jobs, but it swaps them between the two features.

quiz.q: Which pair of statements is matched correctly?
choices: Content explorer shows label changes by users; Activity explorer shows where labeled files are
Compliance score measures security posture; Secure Score measures regulatory progress
Encryption can be reversed with the right key; hashing is designed to be one-way
Microsoft Sentinel is an XDR suite for endpoints; Defender XDR is a cloud-native SIEM
quiz.explain: Encryption turns data into ciphertext that the right key can turn back, while a hash is a fixed-length value that cannot be reversed to the original. Choice A is tempting because both explorers are real Purview tools, but it swaps them: Content explorer shows what exists and where, and Activity explorer shows what was done.

days.recap: SC-900 is 45 minutes with a scaled pass mark of 700 and an unpublished question count; drill the confused pairs across all four domains, keep an error log, answer every item, and know the 24-hour and 14-day retake waits.
